lesson.text: Quick memory: the earthquake drill has three words. What are they? (Drop, cover, hold on.) Today: earthquakes, floods, lightning and heat.
While it shakes, stay inside. The floor moves under your feet, and tiles and glass can fall by doors and windows. Down low under something strong is safest.
No table near? Get down by an inside wall, away from windows, and cover your head and neck with your arms.
Afterwards, walk out to open ground, away from buildings, trees and power lines. Smaller shakes, aftershocks, can follow: drop and cover again.
Flood water: turn around. Just 15 cm of fast water can knock you over. Never walk, play or cycle in it.
Thunder: get inside a building or a car, never under a lone tree. Heat: shade, water and rest in the hottest hours.
Try it in the world: open the practice room, the park and the flooded path. Next: being ready for anything, on the Big track.

choices: stay inside: drop, cover, hold on
exercises.explain: Stay inside: drop, cover, hold on.

exercises.prompt: Fast water flows across the path. You...
exercises.explain: Turn around: never into flood water.

exercises.prompt: A lone tree is a safe place in a thunderstorm.
exercises.explain: False: lightning often strikes tall things. Go inside.

exercises.prompt: No table nearby when it shakes. You...
choices: get down by an inside wall and cover your head
exercises.explain: Down by an inside wall, away from windows, head and neck covered.

exercises.prompt: How deep must fast flood water be to knock you over?
exercises.explain: Only about 15 cm of fast water can knock you over.

exercises.prompt: An earthquake: put it in order.
exercises.explain: Drop, cover, hold on; wait until it stops; then walk out to open ground.

exercises.prompt: After an earthquake, smaller shakes called aftershocks can come.
exercises.explain: True: drop and cover again if one comes.

exercises.prompt: Open ground after an earthquake means...
choices: away from buildings, trees and power lines
exercises.explain: Away from anything that could fall: buildings, trees, power lines.

items: shade and water on a hot day
getting into a car in a storm
exercises.explain: Shade, water and a car in a storm are safe; the midday sun and flood water are not.

exercises.prompt: Why not run outside while it shakes?
choices: things fall by doors and windows
exercises.explain: Tiles and glass can fall by doors and windows, and the floor moves under you.

exercises.prompt: On a very hot day, the hottest hours are the best time for a long run.
exercises.explain: False: rest in the shade in the hottest hours, and drink water.
